rawProteinPurgeSources.name: Raw Chicken & Turkey Cutlets / Whole Bird Purge
rawProteinPurgeSources.dripCapillarityRating: Extreme (Watery protein saline exudate migrates effortlessly along plastic wrap seams)
rawProteinPurgeSources.description: Raw poultry exudate contains the highest pathogen density of all culinary proteins. Salmonella and Campylobacter readily survive at 3°C–4°C in liquid protein matrices.

rawProteinPurgeSources.name: Raw Ground Beef & Minced Red Meat Purge
rawProteinPurgeSources.primaryPathogens: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC O157:H7) & Salmonella
rawProteinPurgeSources.dripCapillarityRating: High (Myoglobin and intracellular fluid pooling in absorbent pad overflow)
rawProteinPurgeSources.description: Ground beef processing distributes surface bacteria throughout the meat mass. Purge fluid contains concentrated STEC capable of causing hemolytic uremic syndrome with an infectious dose as low as 10–100 organisms.

rawProteinPurgeSources.name: Raw Fish Fillets, Whole Salmon & Shellfish Liquor
rawProteinPurgeSources.primaryPathogens: Listeria monocytogenes, Vibrio parahaemolyticus & Psychrotrophic Spoilage Pseudomonas
rawProteinPurgeSources.dripCapillarityRating: Very High (Thin ocean water and melting ice glaze seep across shelf perimeters)
rawProteinPurgeSources.description: Seafood liquor harbors Listeria monocytogenes, which thrives and actively replicates even at sub-zero refrigeration temperatures (-0.4°C / 31.3°F).

rawProteinPurgeSources.name: Raw Pork Chops & Tenderloin Purge
rawProteinPurgeSources.dripCapillarityRating: High (Free-flowing exudate pooling beneath plastic shrink film)
rawProteinPurgeSources.description: Yersinia enterocolitica is psychrotrophic and multiplies efficiently at 4°C, producing acute gastroenteritis mimicking appendicitis in young children.

shelfDesigns.name: Coated Steel Open Wire Grid Shelving (Zero Barrier)
shelfDesigns.capillarySpreadRisk: Catastrophic (Liquid cascades vertically straight through intermediate racks to produce bins)
shelfDesigns.cleanabilityIndex: Poor (Weld junctions, wire corners, and shelf clips harbor bacterial biofilms)
shelfDesigns.description: Budget and garage refrigerators feature open wire racks. When meat leaks, gravity pulls 100% of liquid exudate directly onto foods stored on lower shelves.

shelfDesigns.name: Flat Tempered Glass without Raised Spill Lips
shelfDesigns.capillarySpreadRisk: Moderate-High (Liquid spreads laterally until surface tension breaks at perimeter edge seams)
shelfDesigns.cleanabilityIndex: Good (Smooth non-porous glass sheet cleans easily with disinfectant wipe)
shelfDesigns.description: Standard glass shelves contain small incidental drips via surface tension, but liquid exceeding 15–20 mL cascades down the perimeter side brackets and rear wall.

shelfDesigns.name: SpillGuard Encapsulated Rimmed Tempered Glass Shelf
shelfDesigns.capillarySpreadRisk: Very Low (Raised hydrophobic gasket perimeter retains up to 12 oz of fluid without overflow)
shelfDesigns.cleanabilityIndex: Excellent (Seamless silicone/polypropylene encapsulated perimeter eliminates crannies)
shelfDesigns.description: Engineered spill-proof shelves feature molded hydrophobic edges that hold up to 350 mL (12 oz) of liquid, preventing vertical cascade contamination to lower tiers.

shelfDesigns.name: Sealed Bottom Crisper Drawer Basin
shelfDesigns.capillarySpreadRisk: Extreme Internal Spread (Liquid pools across flat bottom in direct contact with produce)
shelfDesigns.cleanabilityIndex: Moderate (Requires full drawer removal and disinfection of roller tracks and humidity louvers)
shelfDesigns.description: Drawers prevent cascade to the refrigerator floor, but if meat is mistakenly placed inside, poultry purge pools around raw salad greens and fruit, creating 100% surface inoculation.

refrigeratorZoning.name: Top Refrigerator Shelf (Ready-to-Eat Zone)
refrigeratorZoning.fanAirflowExposure: High (Directly in front of top discharge plenum)
refrigeratorZoning.appropriateFoods: Leftovers, cooked meats, ready-to-eat salads, beverages
refrigeratorZoning.rawMeatRiskLevel: Critical Hazard (Top elevation allows gravity to contaminate 100% of refrigerator tiers)
refrigeratorZoning.description: The top shelf has stable temperatures and should strictly store foods consumed without a subsequent cooking kill step. Raw meat stored here violates USDA FSIS food safety standards.

refrigeratorZoning.name: Middle Refrigerator Shelf (Dairy & Prepared Foods)
refrigeratorZoning.appropriateFoods: Dairy products (milk, yogurt, sour cream, hard cheeses), eggs, opened jars
refrigeratorZoning.rawMeatRiskLevel: High Hazard (Directly above lower shelf and crisper bins)
refrigeratorZoning.description: Optimal thermal stability for pasteurized dairy. Storing raw proteins here risks catastrophic drip into fruit and vegetable crispers directly beneath.

refrigeratorZoning.name: Bottom Refrigerator Shelf (Coldest Thermal Zone)
refrigeratorZoning.appropriateFoods: Designated raw poultry, meats, and seafood (MUST be placed in secondary rimmed tray)
refrigeratorZoning.rawMeatRiskLevel: Standard Safe Practice (Lowest gravitational elevation above crisper bins)
refrigeratorZoning.description: The bottom shelf is the coldest region (33°F–36°F / 0.5°C–2.2°C). Dense cold air minimizes psychrotrophic bacterial replication. Placing raw meats here inside a leak-proof rimmed catch pan prevents all vertical drip cascades.

refrigeratorZoning.name: Refrigerator Door Bins (Warmest & Most Fluctuation)
refrigeratorZoning.fanAirflowExposure: Variable (Ambient air ingress during door swings)
refrigeratorZoning.appropriateFoods: Condiments, mustard, high-acid salad dressings, sodas, butter
refrigeratorZoning.rawMeatRiskLevel: Severe Temperature Danger (Exceeds 40°F bacterial danger zone ceiling)
refrigeratorZoning.description: Door bins fluctuate up to 8°C–10°C every time the refrigerator is opened. Never store raw meat, raw poultry, milk, or eggs in door racks.

convectionFanDispersal.name: Multi-Flow Forced Convection Inverter Fan (Modern Frost-Free)
convectionFanDispersal.uncoveredProduceDepositionRisk: Critical (Airborne droplet nuclei settle across uncovered salads and cut melon within 90 minutes)
convectionFanDispersal.description: High-velocity circulation fans prevent frost but transform exposed liquid droplets and drying meat juices into aerosolized droplet nuclei (1–5 µm) that travel across compartments.

convectionFanDispersal.name: Standard Thermostatic Intermittent Fan (15m On / 30m Off Cycles)
convectionFanDispersal.uncoveredProduceDepositionRisk: High (Fan startup bursts aerosolize surface bio-films from evaporator trays and shelf corners)
convectionFanDispersal.description: Periodic air bursts create cyclic pressure differentials that pick up desiccated pathogen particles and circulate them onto uncovered leftovers.

convectionFanDispersal.name: Static Natural Convection Cold-Plate (Manual Defrost)
convectionFanDispersal.uncoveredProduceDepositionRisk: Low Aerosol / High Ceiling Condensation Drip (Moisture beads fall from cold ceiling plate)
convectionFanDispersal.description: Natural thermal convection produces near-zero airborne aerosol dispersal, but elevated humidity promotes heavy ceiling and wall condensation drips.

targetReceptorFoods.name: Sliced Cantaloupe, Honeydew & Watermelon (Uncovered / Clingwrap)
targetReceptorFoods.pathogenProliferationFactor: Extreme (Neutral pH and high sugars support rapid Listeria and Salmonella replication)
targetReceptorFoods.description: Cut melons are the classic high-risk vehicle for foodborne Listeria outbreaks. The flesh has high water activity and neutral pH, allowing single bacterial cells to multiply into infectious doses within 48 hours.

targetReceptorFoods.name: Washed Salad Greens, Baby Spinach & Fresh Herbs in Open Crisper
targetReceptorFoods.pathogenProliferationFactor: Very High (Pathogens enter open leaf stomata and cut vascular stems)
targetReceptorFoods.clinicalSeverity: Severe Bloody Diarrhea / Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)
targetReceptorFoods.description: Leafy greens provide microscopic crevices and open cut stems where Campylobacter and E. coli O157:H7 bind tenaciously via polysaccharide fibrils, resisting cold-water rinsing.

targetReceptorFoods.name: Soft Unpasteurized Cheese (Brie, Camembert, Queso Fresco) & Sliced Deli Ham
targetReceptorFoods.pathogenProliferationFactor: Severe (High protein and fat matrix protects Listeria from cold stress)
targetReceptorFoods.clinicalSeverity: Spontaneous Fetal Loss in Pregnancy / Severe Listeria Sepsis
targetReceptorFoods.description: Deli meats and soft cheeses are ideal psychrotrophic growth substrates. Listeria monocytogenes doubles every 24–36 hours at 4°C (39°F) in these rich protein-lipid matrices.

targetReceptorFoods.name: Airtight Glass Snapware or Hermetic Mason Jar
targetReceptorFoods.pathogenProliferationFactor: Zero Internal Penetration (External surface contamination only)
targetReceptorFoods.postContaminationKillStep: Wiping exterior jar rim with sanitizing wipe before opening
targetReceptorFoods.clinicalSeverity: Minimal (Food inside remains 100% sterile and uncontaminated)
targetReceptorFoods.description: Hermetic glass and rigid BPA-free plastic containers with elastomeric silicone gasket seals provide an impenetrable physical barrier against drips and bio-aerosols.

disinfectantEfficacy.name: Dilute Household Bleach Solution (200 ppm / 1 tbsp Unscented Bleach per Gallon Cool Water)
disinfectantEfficacy.listeriaBiofilmEradication: Complete (Hypochlorous acid penetrates bacterial cell wall and disrupts ribosomal enzymes)
disinfectantEfficacy.description: The gold standard hospital-grade and food-processing sanitizer. At 200 ppm free chlorine, it provides a 5.8-log reduction against Salmonella, Campylobacter, and Listeria within 90 seconds without requiring a post-rinse.

disinfectantEfficacy.name: Commercial Kitchen Disinfectant Spray (Dual-Chain Quat / Benzalkonium Chloride)
disinfectantEfficacy.description: Highly effective against vegetative bacteria, but requires a strict 10-minute wet dwell time to achieve certified kill rates and MUST be thoroughly rinsed with clean water before direct food contact.

disinfectantEfficacy.name: 3% Stabilized Aqueous Hydrogen Peroxide Spray
disinfectantEfficacy.listeriaBiofilmEradication: Moderate-High (Hydroxyl free radicals oxidize cellular proteins with zero toxic fumes)
disinfectantEfficacy.description: Excellent non-toxic alternative. Breaks down into harmless water and oxygen. Eliminates refrigerator odors while achieving > 4-log kill on meat-contact surfaces in 5 minutes.

disinfectantEfficacy.name: Distilled White Vinegar (5% Acetic Acid / Domestic Home Remedy)
disinfectantEfficacy.listeriaBiofilmEradication: Unacceptable / Ineffective (Listeria monocytogenes expresses acid-tolerance response proteins in cold)
disinfectantEfficacy.description: DANGEROUS MISCONCEPTION: Vinegar is NOT an EPA-registered sanitizer for raw meat contamination. Listeria readily adapts to mild acidity (pH 4.0–5.0) at cold temperatures. Vinegar leaves over 2,500 live pathogen cells per square inch.

disinfectantEfficacy.name: Warm Water & Dish Soap Wipe (Surfactant Detergent Only)
disinfectantEfficacy.listeriaBiofilmEradication: Negligible (Physically mobilizes bacteria into cleaning rag, spreading contamination across next shelf)
disinfectantEfficacy.description: Soap dissolves surface grease and loosens dirt, but does NOT kill Salmonella or Listeria. Using a sponge or cloth without follow-up disinfectant spreads pathogens across the entire refrigerator interior.
